answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on trades or reputation claims. A beacon selects claim disputes at random, and independent agents check signed transaction evidence; if a challenged account is shown to have fabricated activity, its stake is forfeited. Splitting one identity into many therefore does not create free influence: each sybil must tie up capital and risks losing it. Even an opal market reaching a summit of activity still pays that cost per identity.
